Baby Hearts in Crisis - Eastern Cape Paediatric Cardio Crisis

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
PE Provisional Cath Lab, the only Cath Lab in the Eastern Cape, has been broken since October 2018
A Cath Lab is used for Angiograms and to treat blood clots (strokes) and children diagnosed with Congenital heart disease. In Feb alone over 40 pediatric patients were turned away

The biggest crises is children diagnosed with Congenital heart disease. VSD is diagnosed at birth and can be easily repaired in a Cath Lab, but because the Cath Labs are broken these children are having to have open heart surgery. The problem with that is that the waiting list for open heart is 2/3 years, which has been exasperated by the broken Cath Lab. When a VSD is not fixed and the patient has to wait they eventually get pulmonary hypertension (narrowing of the passages from the heart to the lungs) which means they are pushed forward for emergency surgery.
Due to a lack of resources these children are dying from what is a very simply treatable disorder.
Stats for SA as a whole: 8000 children are born a year with VSD
3-5 born in the Nelson Mandela Bay per month


Further information:
Machine broke in October, 3 days later the funds were given to local government by provisional to buy new equipment. In January the MEC lied to legislator and said that the equipment had been purchased and would arrive Feb.
It has now however been purchased and will arrive end of March, but then it will take an uncertain amount of time to get up and running again.
Department keeps saying critical patients will be sent to private, not one patient has gone to private as there no official agreement has been made with netcare as yet.
Not a new problem, machines have been breaking on and off for at least 3 years.
Adele Greyling, head of Pediatric cardiology went to Amsterdam to specialise in Electrophysiology, a machine that can fix rhythmic heart issues, which if left untreated can cause a heart attack. She convinced a supplier to loan the machines, but when the cath lab broke they took the machines back and the department has no plan to actually purchase any.

Case studies so far

Joshua
He was born with half a heart and has had multiple surgeries. The only surgery he had that wasn't done by Adele was a failure and he was in a critical condition.
Currently he is waiting for the 3rd part of a 3 part operation to fix is oxygen saturation levels, which he can't have due to there being no Cath lab. ultimately he needs a new heart. String case study, because he is now 9 and has been in Pediatric cardiology system since he was born and has been treated by Adele the whole time.

I am waiting to speak to Adele this evening for the stronger case studies of patients who are now waiting for surgery. The ones I have are not critical enough.

Script:


Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
1 00:00 Voice over State patients in the Eastern Cape in desperate need of cardiac treatment are
in a crisis as the facilities needed to keep them alive are simply not available
2 00:10 Luis Everybody likes to think they are going to get help because we are all human and we like to think you know that they are going to make us better but they just leave us to die like cattle
3 00:20 Voice over A crucial part of keeping cardiology patients alive is a catheterization lab.

4 00:26 Link Devi In the Eastern Cape, up until October last year, there was one lab, in the
public sector, for over 6 million people. But that lab is no longer functional
5 00:37 Voice over And it has not been functional for 6 months. Dr Kettles is a private cardiologist who commits his time to state facilities like
the Frere in East-London.
6 00:47 Dr Kettles A catheterization laboratory is a specialised theatre essentially, it’s a basic tool for a cardiologist today and its used for diagnosis of heart disease
7 00:59 Voice over A Cath lab is also used for life saving surgical Procedures done on the heart,
none of which can currently be performed in the Eastern Cape
8 01:08 Dr Kettles To do a ward round at the local state hospital and be presented with a few patients have a critical for cardiac surgery and that’s pretty demoralizing
9 01:23 Voice over Currently cardiac patients in the Eastern Cape are given basic medication and left hoping for the best
10 01:28 Dr Kettles The geographic injustice of it is what really drives us just about to tears.
11 01:32 Voice over After experiencing severe chest pains Luis Luzada was rushed to a state
facility and diagnosed with a heart attack
12 01:40 Luiz We waited there for help from about 14:00 in the afternoon to about 19:00 o’clock at night. Eventually we got a bed and they just left me for days, people next me they all got the same problem as I have I could see that cos I spoke to them and they are all in pain no treatment and help came
13 02:00 Voice over Luis was at Frere for 4 days without being seen by a cardiologist until his relative came and demanded to get clear answers
14 02:08 Jane So, the doctor said to me that he needs an angiogram
15 02:11 Voice over An Angiogram is diagnostic test done in a Cath Lab that takes pictures inside the heart
16 02:17 Jane I was like well this is wonderful, is he booked in? or what’s happening with the angiogram? The doctor said “can’t have an angiogram done here in East London” and I said ‘why? ‘and he said “we just don’t have a Cath lab facilities” and so I said to him “right, what’s the next point of call? Where is the next available machine for Luiz to have an angiogram?” and the doctor advice in PE but we are wasting our time because the angiogram in PE is broken and the doctor advised we are not allowed to transfer out your province. What does that leave Luiz with?
16 02:55 Luiz The doctor then said you know they can only do so much a not more and that’s how they left me.
17 03:02 Voice over DR Pepeta was the head of Paediatric cardiology at PE provincial until the end
of 2017. He still does sessions there and is gravely concerned for children born with congenital heart disease who will require treatment within a Cath Lab within the first month of their lives
18 03:19 Devi and Dr Pepeta Devi: and what happens to those children? Cos now we have a situation where there is no provincial Cath lab?

Dr. Pepeta: They get admitted in the ward, they get medication, nothing is not done and they get infections and if they are lucky they will get another central hospital
Devi: That’s in another province
Dr. Pepeta: I know what else can one do? If you got these patients that are dying before. So, they go there and they may not always get there so again they will die
19 03:49 Voice over When he was only 5 months old Joshua was Diagnosed with severe congenital heart disease, which required immediate treatment in a Cath Lab. His foster mom Elmarie Van Rensburg took him to PE Provincial
20 04:02 Elmarie Elmarie: When they had him in a Cath lab they realized that he’s actually not going to make it so they sent him straight to ICU and did emergency heart surgery the next day to put in a shunt. Yeah it was world wind ride
Devi: If Joshua was born at a time where there were no Cath labs would he have survived?
Elmarie: No. no absolutely not
21 04:24 Video of Joshua
22 04:29 Elmarie and Devi Elmarie: Yeah dealing with fear is quit a big thing because you know it can change at any stage cos so many things are out of your control so all you can do is make sure that he gets the best care that’s available and now we can’t access that, not here
23 04:46 Voice over The Cath Lab in PE Provincial didn’t just stop working overnight, it had slowly been giving issues over the past few years.
24 04:53 Devi and HOD of Health Dr Mbengashe Dr. Mbengashe: The life span of a Cath lab is 7 – 10 years and that Cath lab hit its 10th year in 2015/2016
Devi: Already?
Dr. Mbengashe: No, it’s a mind-boggling state of affairs.
25 05:08 Voice over Dr Thobela Mbengashe Is the Head of department for the depart of the Eastern Cape
26 05:13 Devi and HOD of Health Dr Mbengashe Devi: Were you aware that there were maintenance issues over the past couple of years?
Dr. Mbengashe: Yes, we were aware but the Cath lab was still within its life span but we know that once the frequency of breakdowns and maintenance come in then there’s a problem.
Devi: I was given to understand that around 2015 already it was on its last year at that point
Dr. Mbengashe: that’s not the point, the key thing is that as long as its functional and does the job and its safe its providing community with care it’s still very useable
27 05:44 Link – Devi When a baby is born with congenital heart disease that requires intervention,
a Cath lab provides a fairly simple fix. But without one, babies have to undergo open heart surgery and the waiting list in the Eastern Cape is two to three years.
28 05:59 Devi and HOD of Health Dr Mbengashe Devi: The waiting list for open heart surgery is allegedly between 2-3 years is that true?
Dr. Mbengashe: We don’t do open heart surgeries
Devi: At all?
Dr. Mbengashe: At all, we don’t have the capability. We send our patients to Red Cross
29 06:13 Dr Kettles I’m not sure if the HOD meant there is currently no heart surgery being performed in state hospitals cos I believe that’s true, but that has not always been the case. Port Elizabeth has had a very active surgical unit for many many years
30 06:28 Voice over In Feb alone paediatric cardiology turned away 40 patients desperate for treatment. There is no clear list of Adult patients waiting for access, but these numbers are continuously increasing.
31 06:45 Dr Kettles If you look at the big cities where things are working pretty well there’s 2 state Cath labs in Cape Town – Grooteshuur Hospital and Tygerburg Hospital. My understand is that those 2 units together do round about 3000 angiographic procedures a year that’s still a very large number considering the Eastern Cape is a slightly bigger population than that. we are doing non-for our state patients.
32 07:08 Voice over After receiving no treatment Luis’s family made an emergency appointment with DR Kettles at his private practice who told them they would need over 100 000 rand for an Angiogram and treatment
33 07:20 Jane Dr Kettles says you have to find a way to raise this money. He says Luiz is basically a ticking time bomb.
34 07:28 Voice over The family was given 48 hours to find the money
35 07:32 Jane We managed to raise the funds within the 48 hours and they took Luiz in for the procedure on Monday. And when Dr. Kettles came out the procedure room, he said he actually doesn’t know how Luiz live the weekend he must’ve had a guardian angels. He had over 90% narrowing of the arteries in the heart and he said he was a dead man walking.
36 07:59 Voice over Joshua was due to have the final part of a 3-part operation to increase his oxygen saturation levels. but that has been put on hold indefinitely, as the Cath lab is broken.
37 08:09 Elmarie doing oxygen tests on Joshua A healthy person should be around 100 and anything from 97 – 98 – 100. Should you be ill with bronchitis or pneumonia or something and your stats drop below 90 they will hospitalize you but he’s normal right now is sort of between 75 and 85 %.
As a heart mom you are always going, then you don’t sleep, you listen to the breathing you make sure they are okay, you check the stats. Yeah in the past if needed too I could rush up to the hospital and now… sorry we can’t
38 08:57 Devi and HOD of Health Dr Mbengashe Devi: Why is it that we are stuck in this period right now where we don’t have a functioning Cath lab within the system?
Dr. Mbengashe: That’s very important. What usually happens is the…, when this one ended and it wasn’t working the next is to get another one to replace it which we have done, to get another one. We have built another service in the new Nelson Mandela academic where we have the latest Cath lab
Devi: Let’s talk about the one in Mthatha, is it working? Is it in operation?
Dr. Mbengashe: It’s in operation, but it’s not fully functional in terms of its capability.
Devi: Then we can’t say it’s in operational then
Dr. Mbengashe: No, it is in operation,
Devi: So, what do you mean? The child is born with congenital heart defect? So, the child will be transported to Mthatha? And will be able to perform the necessary procedures?
Dr. Mbengashe: The point I’m trying to make, this is the point I’m making is that the Cath lab has multiple functions and some of them can be done and some of them can sophisticated…
Devi: I get that because I don’t want us to talk spin here, I want us to get to the bottom of this
Dr. Mbengashe: I train as a doctor and you can only talk truth.
39 10:12 Dr Kettles Is Mthatha fully functional? To my knowledge certainly not and I think we would know. We would be the first in line to sending them patients and we have not such offer and in my direct communications I’m not aware of it being functional at all from the few patients done at the opening for the press.
40 10:31 Voice over Mthatha may have all of the equipment, but it does not have the staff requirements needed to operate as an solution to the Cath Lab that stopped being functional in PE Provincial over 6 months ago. But the health department have been saying a new Cath has been ordered for months that last date given was mid-February
41 10:51 Devi and HOD of Health Dr Mbengashe Dr. Mbengashe: Actually, the fully functioning Cath lab is going to be in place in the next 9 weeks, it will be here on the 29th it will be delivered and in 9 weeks’ time it will be functioning.
Devi: it still doesn’t explain the fact that we have a gap and that we do not have a fully functioning Cath lab that’s owned by the state
42 11:09 Dr Pepeta and Devi interview Dr. Pepeta: A new born with a blocked vessel doesn’t have a couple of months, has a day or 2. And if you have a heart attack and needed a scan, if I were to survive or you’ll die from your heart attack
43 11:21 Dr. Kettles It is unacceptable for us to deliver 1970’s level of cardiac care to our population
44 11:27 Devi and HOD of Health Dr Mbengashe Devi: You are the HOD of this department?
Dr. Mbengashe: Yes
Devi: Are you satisfied that you did your best?
Dr. Mbengashe: yes,
Devi: Can you guarantee that nobody has died in this province because there has been no Cath lab, fully functioning Cath lab
Dr Mbengashe: What I can guarantee is that anyone that needs urgent attention
Devi: You are not answering the question
Dr. Mbengashe: because I wouldn’t really know
Devi: Then say that I wouldn’t really know it’s okay I don’t expect you to know everything.
Dr. Mbengashe: I wouldn’t really know.
45 11:58 Devi and Dr. Pepeta Devi: Are patients dying as a result of the closing of the provincial Cath lab?
Dr. Pepeta: yeah, I mean that’s no brainer that is happening, it is what it is

metadata.Summary: PE Provisional Cath Lab, the only Cath Lab in the Eastern Cape, has been broken since October 2018 A Cath Lab is used for Angiograms and to treat blood clots (strokes) and children diagnosed with Congenital heart disease. In Feb alone over 40 pediatric patients were turned away The biggest crises is children diagnosed with Congenital heart disease. VSD is diagnosed at birth and can be easily repaired in a Cath Lab, but because the Cath Labs are broken these children are having to have open heart surgery. The problem with that is that the waiting list for open heart is 2/3 years, which has been exasperated by the broken Cath Lab. When a VSD is not fixed and the patient has to wait they eventually get pulmonary hypertension (narrowing of the passages from the heart to the lungs) which means they are pushed forward for emergency surgery. Due to a lack of resources these children are dying from what is a very simply treatable disorder. Stats for SA as a whole: 8000 children are born a year with VSD 3-5 born in the Nelson Mandela Bay per month
metadata.Further information: Machine broke in October, 3 days later the funds were given to local government by provisional to buy new equipment. In January the MEC lied to legislator and said that the equipment had been purchased and would arrive Feb. It has now however been purchased and will arrive end of March, but then it will take an uncertain amount of time to get up and running again. Department keeps saying critical patients will be sent to private, not one patient has gone to private as there no official agreement has been made with netcare as yet. Not a new problem, machines have been breaking on and off for at least 3 years. Adele Greyling, head of Pediatric cardiology went to Amsterdam to specialise in Electrophysiology, a machine that can fix rhythmic heart issues, which if left untreated can cause a heart attack. She convinced a supplier to loan the machines, but when the cath lab broke they took the machines back and the department has no plan to actually purchase any. Case studies so far Joshua He was born with half a heart and has had multiple surgeries. The only surgery he had that wasn't done by Adele was a failure and he was in a critical condition. Currently he is waiting for the 3rd part of a 3 part operation to fix is oxygen saturation levels, which he can't have due to there being no Cath lab. ultimately he needs a new heart. String case study, because he is now 9 and has been in Pediatric cardiology system since he was born and has been treated by Adele the whole time. I am waiting to speak to Adele this evening for the stronger case studies of patients who are now waiting for surgery. The ones I have are not critical enough.
